body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. Saturday arrives with a mild, hazy start — 55 degrees at Meadows Field and a high near 80 on the way — as the community continues to mourn 16-year-old William Aviles, remembered at a vigil Friday night nearly a week after he was killed at a Halloween party. Air quality sits at a moderate 80, no weather alerts are active, and deputies spent the overnight hours on a shooting call near 7th Standard Road, a stabbing report at a trailer park, and a pair of fires.

## The Kern Overnight

The night's most serious call came from the county side of 7th Standard Road, where deputies were sent at 10:43 p.m. to the area of Mayer Avenue for shots fired. A caller told dispatchers two people were shooting and trying to shoot his brother, and deputies reported no injuries so far but said the suspects might still be in the area and that a victim was hiding in a field nearby. A drone was requested, and by 11:01 p.m. deputies had begun searching for shell casings.

Deputies were back out about three hours later at the Edison Trailer Park on Edison Highway, where a 17-year-old was reported to have been hit with glass and suffered facial injuries. The man suspected in that assault left on foot before deputies arrived.

Earlier in the evening, fire crews and medics were sent at 7:25 p.m. to Edison Highway westbound at Fairfax Road north, where a vehicle hit a juvenile and left one patient down in the roadway. A domestic disturbance at 10:28 p.m. ended with the man who threatened the caller walking out before officers got there.

Two burglaries in progress stood out in the log: a man in a black hooded sweatshirt caught on camera at the Dollar Tree on the 2,500 block of South 8th Street at 8:32 p.m., and a man on a bicycle seen on camera at a Toyota dealership at 4:59 a.m. Fire crews also ran a working fire behind a home on the 5,500 block of Woodmere Drive in southwest Bakersfield at 12:48 a.m., smoke reported inside a one-story apartment complex on the 1,600 block of East 11th Street in east Bakersfield at 3:58 a.m., and vehicle fires on Panama Road and Muller Road in southeast Bakersfield.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 80 degrees today and a low around 53 tonight, according to the National Weather Service. It's currently 55 degrees at Meadows Field. No active weather alerts are in place for Kern County, and no active fires are being reported. Air quality is 80 — moderate — so most people can be outside comfortably, though those sensitive to smoke or dust may want to keep an eye on conditions through the afternoon. A warm, quiet November Saturday is on tap across the valley.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that friends, family and neighbors returned to South Half Moon Drive to honor 16-year-old William Aviles, shot and killed during a house party in the early morning hours of Halloween.** Those who gathered remembered a teen his friends describe as someone who could brighten anyone's day. Aviles had recently transferred to Centennial High School, where classmates say his absence has left a classroom feeling empty. Kern Secret Witness is now offering a reward of up to $20,000 for information leading to an arrest and prosecution, and investigators say they've received limited information from the public and are hoping to hear from people who were at the party.

**KGET 17 reports that two people were struck by a hit-and-run driver on Edison Highway, and one of them has died, according to the California Highway Patrol.** The crash fits into a stretch of Edison Highway that saw multiple emergency calls overnight, including the juvenile struck near Fairfax Road. The CHP's investigation is ongoing, and the brief did not include further details about the driver or the victims.

**According to 23ABC, more than a dozen senior citizens living at the Palm Motel in Delano are at risk of becoming homeless after the city red-tagged and condemned the property on October 27.** Tenants describe plumbing problems, a pest infestation, black mold, exposed wiring and no working electricity after power was shut off following an inspection — conditions that are especially hard on residents with asthma who say they can't even plug in their nebulizers. The city gave residents until November 7 to leave, but tenants on fixed incomes say they have nowhere to go and can't afford another place. City officials say they are working to avoid pushing people into homelessness.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Governor Newsom plans to commute all California death row sentences, a decision that affects Kern County.** The move would reshape the state's most serious criminal cases, including those prosecuted here, and is expected to draw strong reaction from local officials and victims' families in the days ahead.

**KGET 17 also reports that temporary sidewalks put in during downtown construction are proving nice in some places and non-existent in others.** The patchwork of walkways has left pedestrians navigating an uneven path through the work zone, a small but daily frustration for people who live and work downtown.

## Something good

23ABC is holding a Community Baby Shower on November 19, collecting donations for the Bakersfield Pregnancy Center. The center provides expecting Kern County families with free resources — pregnancy tests, ultrasounds and confidential consultations — and hosts a baby shower each quarter to supply parents in need with diapers, formula and clothing. 23ABC has partnered with the center since 2018, and donations can be dropped off at the station, 321 21st Street in downtown Bakersfield, from 5 a.m. to 7 p.m. that day.

## Coming up this week

The week ahead brings a pair of public meetings on Monday, November 9. The Fire Civil Service Commission meets at 3 p.m., and the Youth Commission meets at 4:30 p.m. Both are open to the public, and agendas are typically posted ahead of time on the city's website.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a busy stretch. Journey USA takes the stage tonight, November 7, with TEXAS TORNADO TRADITION also playing the Fox the same evening. The 2026 Golden Empire Youth Cheer EXPO fills the theater on Sunday, November 8, and the Cults & Classics series continues Monday, November 9, with a screening of "Play Misty for Me." Looking a little further out, NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives at the Fox on November 13, and a Cults & Classics season pass for 2026-2027 is already on sale.

Also worth noting: the CIF Central Section playoffs open their first round this week, with scores and matchups tracked by KGET 17's 17 Scoreboard. And if you're planning to donate to the 23ABC Community Baby Shower, November 19 is the date to circle — it's a chance to help local families who could use a hand.

top.title: Community gathers for vigil honoring 16-year-old Bakersfield teen shot and killed at Halloween party
